text: An operations lead wants to integrate Claude into an existing invoice-processing workflow that currently takes analysts 2 hours per batch. The team wants Claude to draft summaries of flagged discrepancies for human review, not to approve payments. Which approach best reflects sound workflow integration practice?
options: Replace the human review step entirely and let Claude approve payments automatically to save time
Avoid using Claude in this workflow since financial processes should never involve AI tools
Use Claude only to generate marketing announcements about the new process, without touching the actual workflow
Use Claude to generate discrepancy summaries that analysts review and approve before any payment action is taken
correct_answer: Use Claude to generate discrepancy summaries that analysts review and approve before any payment action is taken
explanation: Sound workflow integration augments existing processes rather than fully replacing human judgment in high-stakes decisions like payment approval. Claude can accelerate the drafting and summarization step while preserving a human-in-the-loop checkpoint for final decisions (D), balancing efficiency with risk management. Fully automating approvals (A) removes necessary oversight, avoiding Claude entirely (B) ignores a legitimate efficiency opportunity, and (C) is irrelevant to the operational workflow.

text: A project manager is presenting a proposal to senior leadership to adopt Claude for drafting status reports across teams. One executive asks about the risks of relying on AI-generated content. What is the most appropriate way for the project manager to respond?
options: State that Claude never makes mistakes on internal documents, so there are no meaningful risks to address
Acknowledge that outputs require human review for accuracy and context, and explain the validation steps the team will follow
Avoid answering the question since model limitations are a technical topic outside the project manager's responsibility
Suggest that leadership not worry about risks since the AI vendor is legally responsible for all internal report accuracy
correct_answer: Acknowledge that outputs require human review for accuracy and context, and explain the validation steps the team will follow
explanation: Communicating Claude's value and limitations to stakeholders is an explicit objective in workflow integration and solution design. A credible proposal (B) honestly addresses risks such as hallucinations or missing context and explains the team's human validation workflow, rather than overstating capabilities (A), deflecting the question (C), or shifting accountability elsewhere (D).

text: A consultant is helping a client redesign a customer-support triage process. The client currently has agents manually categorize incoming tickets before routing them, which creates delays. The consultant wants to use Claude to support this redesign. Which use of Claude best fits the 'solution design and iteration' objective?
options: Use Claude to propose an initial triage framework, test it against sample tickets, and iteratively refine the categories based on results
Use Claude once to write a final policy document and consider the redesign complete without testing
Ask Claude to replace all human support agents immediately without piloting the new triage categories
Skip using Claude for process design and only use it for drafting internal emails announcing the change
correct_answer: Use Claude to propose an initial triage framework, test it against sample tickets, and iteratively refine the categories based on results
explanation: Solution design is iterative (A): propose an initial design, test it against real or representative sample tickets, and refine based on observed results before full rollout. A one-shot final document (B) skips validation, replacing all agents without a pilot (C) introduces high operational risk, and limiting Claude's role to announcement emails (D) misses the opportunity to use it for solution design.

text: A team is setting up a Claude Project to support quarterly compliance reporting. They want Claude to reference only the most current internal policy documents rather than outdated versions from prior quarters. What is the best configuration practice to follow?
options: Upload every historical policy document version ever created so Claude has maximum historical context
Leave outdated documents in the Project knowledge base since Claude will automatically ignore older versions
Avoid uploading any policy documents and rely only on brief system-level instructions summarizing the rules from memory
Regularly review and update the Project's knowledge sources, removing outdated documents and replacing them with current versions
correct_answer: Regularly review and update the Project's knowledge sources, removing outdated documents and replacing them with current versions
explanation: Maintaining and updating configurations and knowledge sources (D) is a core configuration management objective. Claude does not automatically know which conflicting policy file is authoritative if outdated versions remain in the knowledge base (B), keeping all historical versions (A) invites confusion between old and new rules, and omitting source documents entirely (C) increases the risk of inaccurate recall.

text: A marketing manager connects Claude to the team's Google Drive to allow it to reference shared campaign briefs. After a few weeks, several briefs in the folder are outdated and no longer relevant to current campaigns. What is the most appropriate ongoing configuration practice?
options: Periodically audit the connected folder and remove or archive outdated files so Claude references only current materials
Disconnect the Google Drive connector permanently since connected folders cannot be curated once linked
Leave the connected folder unmanaged since Claude automatically filters out older campaign files
Re-upload all campaign files manually into every chat session every day instead of using the connector

text: A knowledge worker is writing system-level instructions for a Claude Project used to draft customer emails. Which instruction best reflects an effective system-level instruction?
options: "Be helpful and write good customer emails whenever a team member asks."
"Do whatever the user asks in the chat, with no formatting or length constraints."
"Write emails in a friendly, professional tone, keep responses under 150 words, and always include a closing signature with the company name."
"Use the most complex, academic vocabulary possible in every email so the company sounds impressive."
correct_answer: "Write emails in a friendly, professional tone, keep responses under 150 words, and always include a closing signature with the company name."

Vague instructions (A), unconstrained instructions (B), and instructions optimizing for overly complex vocabulary (D) do not provide the structure needed for reliable, on-brand customer emails.

text: An employee wants to use Claude to help draft a performance improvement plan for a specific underperforming team member, including details about the employee's medical leave history to justify the decision. Which response best reflects appropriate use-case judgment?
options: Proceed as planned since Claude can draft any internal HR document requested by a manager
Avoid including sensitive personal health information and consult HR/legal guidance on appropriate handling before using Claude to draft the document
Include the full medical leave details in the prompt, but instruct Claude to keep the health information confidential
Include the medical history in the prompt because chat conversations are automatically invisible to compliance audits
correct_answer: Avoid including sensitive personal health information and consult HR/legal guidance on appropriate handling before using Claude to draft the document

Proceeding as-is (A), asking the model to 'keep it confidential' in a prompt (C), or assuming chats are exempt from governance (D) fails to protect sensitive employee health data.

text: A financial analyst in a regulated industry wants to paste a client's full account statement, including Social Security number, into Claude to get help summarizing spending patterns. Organizational AI policy prohibits sharing regulated personal identifiers with external AI tools. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Paste the unredacted statement as-is since the summary is for internal analysis purposes only
Ask Claude to promise not to store or repeat the Social Security number before pasting the statement
Use a personal, non-work Claude account on a personal device to bypass the organizational restriction
Redact or remove the regulated personal identifiers before submitting the statement, consistent with organizational policy
correct_answer: Redact or remove the regulated personal identifiers before submitting the statement, consistent with organizational policy
explanation: Following organizational AI policy and applying data-sensitivity and regulatory safeguards requires sanitizing or redacting regulated identifiers (such as SSNs) before submission (D). Submitting unredacted PII (A) violates policy regardless of internal intent, asking the model for a promise (B) is not a valid technical or compliance control, and using a personal account to bypass governance (C) is a severe policy violation.

text: A team is deciding whether to use Claude to generate a company-wide policy on remote work eligibility that will materially affect employee compensation and job classification. The decision carries legal and ethical implications for employees. What is the most responsible approach?
options: Let Claude generate the final policy and publish it immediately without human review, since it drafted the text quickly
Use Claude to draft an initial version of the policy, then route it through legal, HR, and leadership review before any decisions affecting employees are finalized
Prohibit any Claude involvement in drafting, since AI tools can never be used to prepare initial HR policy outlines
Have Claude make the final binding eligibility determinations for each individual employee based on their personnel file
correct_answer: Use Claude to draft an initial version of the policy, then route it through legal, HR, and leadership review before any decisions affecting employees are finalized
explanation: Understanding ethical and governance implications of AI usage (B) means recognizing that decisions materially affecting employee compensation or job status require human accountability, legal review, and leadership oversight, even when AI assists with initial drafting. Publishing without review (A) or delegating final individual determinations to the model (D) abdicates human responsibility, while blanket avoidance of drafting assistance (C) overlooks a safe, productive human-in-the-loop use case.
